question: Does removing red muscle-role color from the same complete ecorche geometry cause Flux to infer a continuous outer skin?

cells.observation: Flux preserves exposed muscle and bone roles while repairing local cat anatomy, feet, head, and stance. It does not synthesize a continuous outer skin.

cells.variable: uniform white-clay palette over identical admitted geometry
cells.observation: Flux reinterprets the uniform source as a coherent pale skeletal specimen, adding ribs and bone-like structure. It does not synthesize a continuous outer skin.

result.meaning: At seed 80301, chromatic role separation materially governs how Flux assigns anatomical semantics. Removing it does not reduce source literalism into skin; it changes the inferred anatomical category.
result.claimCeiling: One fixed seed establishes a causal difference between these two palettes on this exact complete geometry. It does not establish generality across seeds, prompts, views, or analytical skin representations.
result.nextAssay: Compare this exact exposed ecorche against a genuinely low-frequency analytical outer skin compiled over the same authored structure, then add a prompt-only neutral plate baseline.
